title: 5 Fonts That Tell Your Viewer How to Feel

slides.heading: Your Font Speaks Before Your Script Does
slides.subtitle: Most editors pick fonts based on what looks cool. The better call is picking based on what the content needs to feel like.
slides.takeaway: Every font choice is a signal your viewer processes before they decide whether to keep watching.
slides.visual: A dark video frame showing five different font styles stacked vertically each radiating a completely different mood and energy, from clean and trustworthy to loud and cinematic. Deep dark purple background, cinematic mood, purple accent light, high contrast, match the brand guide style.

slides.heading: Montserrat
slides.subtitle: The clean, modern workhorse. Signals trustworthiness without feeling corporate. Built for educational content, tutorials, and explainers.
slides.takeaway: Viewers read it as credible before they consciously register the font choice.
slides.visual: The word MONTSERRAT displayed in its own clean sans-serif typeface in large bold letters on a dark screen, with a tutorial subtitle example below showing its professional, approachable presence. Deep dark purple background, cinematic mood, purple accent light, high contrast, match the brand guide style.

slides.heading: Oswald
slides.subtitle: Bold, condensed, no-nonsense. Use when the content needs to hit hard. Business breakdowns, direct-response, authority-first content.
slides.takeaway: Feels like someone who means business, tbh.
slides.visual: The word OSWALD displayed in its own heavy condensed typeface on a dark screen, bold and imposing, with a business-style headline example below showing its authoritative, no-nonsense presence. Deep dark purple background, cinematic mood, purple accent light, high contrast, match the brand guide style.

slides.heading: Playfair Display
slides.subtitle: Elegant, high-contrast, premium. If your content is luxury-adjacent, design-led, or targets a high-income audience, this is the one.
slides.takeaway: Signals quality before the viewer reads a single word.
slides.visual: The words Playfair Display shown in its own elegant high-contrast serif typeface on a dark screen, the letterforms refined and editorial, with a luxury content example below. Deep dark purple background, cinematic mood, purple accent light, high contrast, match the brand guide style.

slides.heading: Bebas Neue
slides.subtitle: Loud, cinematic, built for impact. Sports, action, gaming, hype-style editing. The text itself needs to feel like part of the energy.
slides.takeaway: Use it when you need the words to hit as hard as the visuals.
slides.visual: The words BEBAS NEUE displayed in its own massive all-caps impact typeface filling most of the dark frame, the letters tight and punchy like a sports broadcast graphic, pure visual aggression. Deep dark purple background, cinematic mood, purple accent light, high contrast, match the brand guide style.

slides.heading: DM Sans
slides.subtitle: Minimal, tech-forward, editorial. For productivity content, creator economy posts, anything that needs to feel modern but not aggressive.
slides.takeaway: Readers trust DM Sans the same way they trust a clean, well-designed app. Save this for your next project.
slides.visual: The words DM Sans displayed in its own clean minimal typeface on a dark screen, light and editorial, with a tech-forward content example below showing its modern approachable presence. Deep dark purple background, cinematic mood, purple accent light, high contrast, match the brand guide style.
